author: admin
body: Should we also set up shared TypeScript configs in packages/tsconfig? That would save duplication across workspaces.

author: john
body: Good idea. I'll add a base tsconfig and extend from it. Also considering remote caching with Turborepo — worth discussing.

author: admin
body: Agreed on remote caching. Let's use Vercel's built-in cache for now and revisit if we hit limits.

author: jane
body: Should we apply different limits per role? Admins probably need higher thresholds than regular users.

author: admin
body: Good point. Let's go with 100 req/min for users and 500 for admins. We can tighten later based on usage.

author: john
body: Connection string updated in all environments. The M0 free tier has a 512 MB limit — worth keeping an eye on once real data comes in.

author: admin
body: Already on it. Set up Atlas monitoring alerts at 80% capacity. Should be fine for the foreseeable future.

author: sarah
body: Dev environment is connecting fine. Actually noticing lower latency compared to the local instance — nice side effect.

author: admin
body: Make sure the new guards are composable — we'll need to stack role checks on some routes without duplicating logic.

author: john
body: Implemented as higher-order functions. You can now do requireRole('admin') or requireRole('admin', 'manager'). PR is up for review.

author: jane
body: 300ms feels right for the debounce. Should we also cancel the previous in-flight request when a new one fires?

author: admin
body: TanStack Query handles that automatically with the right queryKey setup — no need for manual AbortControllers.

author: jane
body: Confirmed, works perfectly. Closing the loop on this one — ready for testing.

author: john
body: Reproduced consistently. The redirect to /login clears router state, losing the intended destination. Saving the URL to sessionStorage before redirecting should fix it.

author: sarah
body: Confirmed fix works in my local testing. Also verified with expired tokens — redirect happens cleanly and the user lands back on the right page after re-login.

author: admin
body: Good catch on the approach. Just make sure the saved URL is validated before redirect to avoid open redirect vulnerabilities.

author: jane
body: iOS Safari passes all scenarios. Android Chrome has a slight delay on initial grab — possibly the touch activation constraint being too tight. Testing with 150ms now.

author: john
body: 150ms feels much better on Android. Still seeing occasional snap-back on fast swipes — investigating if it's a collision detection issue.

author: admin
body: First k6 run peaked at 420 concurrent users before response times degraded. The bottleneck appears to be in the task list query — no index on the composite filter fields.

author: john
body: Added compound index on { status, priority, assignedTo }. Re-running the load test — early numbers look much better.

author: admin
body: Second run hit 500 concurrent users with p99 under 200ms. That's acceptable for now. Marking ready to merge.

author: admin
body: Great work using HttpOnly cookies instead of localStorage. Remember we'll need to set SameSite=None when deploying frontend and backend to separate domains.

author: john
body: Already noted in the deployment checklist. Will flip the flag in the auth controller when we set up the prod environment.

author: sarah
body: The fractional indexing approach for rank is clever — avoids reindexing the entire column on every move. Nice.

author: admin
body: Touch support was the tricky part. The 200ms delay on TouchSensor is the sweet spot between accidental drags and intentional ones.

author: jane
body: Tested on iPad and it's smooth. One minor thing — the drag overlay shadow could be slightly stronger for better depth perception. Could be a follow-up.

author: jane
body: Should tags be free-text or a fixed taxonomy? Free-text is faster to ship but gets messy fast.

author: admin
body: Let's start free-text with autocomplete against existing tags — cheap to build, and we can add normalization later if it gets messy.

author: jane
body: Fixed by normalizing to NFC before comparing. "Crème brûlée" and "creme brulee" both need to match now too — using a stripped-accents fallback.
